question.stem:
A company wants to organize the way it tracks its spending on AWS resources. A report that summarizes the total billing accrued by each department must be generated at the end of the month. The company already uses a Savings Plan for pricing, but that does not break down costs by department.
Which solution will meet the requirements?
options: Tag resources with the department name and configure a budget action in AWS Budget.
Tag resources with the department name and enable cost allocation tags.
Use AWS Cost Explorer to view spending and filter usage data by Resource.
Create a Cost and Usage report for AWS services that each department is using.
question.explanation: To break down billing by department you tag resources (e.g. Department=Marketing) and activate that tag key as a cost allocation tag in the Billing console. Only activated tags appear as a dimension in Cost Explorer, Budgets and the Cost and Usage Report, so you can group/filter the monthly bill by department. A budget action automatically applies a policy or stops instances when a threshold is hit — it restricts, it doesn't report. Filtering Cost Explorer by resource shows per-resource spend but has no notion of departments without activated tags. A CUR per service lists line items by service, not by department — it also depends on activated cost allocation tags to group by department.

concept: Cost allocation tags: tag + activate to break down costs by department
tests: Knowing that per-department cost reports need resource tags that are activated as cost allocation tags.
expected: Tag resources with the department and activate the tag as a cost allocation tag (then group by it in Cost Explorer/CUR). Triggers: "report per department / team / project / cost center", "break down costs" → tags + activated cost allocation tags.
why_not: Budget actions enforce limits, not reporting; Cost Explorer by resource ≠ by department without tags; CUR by service doesn't group by department on its own — it needs activated tags too.
